item.title: Factory Ruins Become Park: smokestack becomes Rastin Observation Tower; three lakes surround trails
item.description: Mount Vernon's Ariel-Foundation Park now spans 250 acres, blending industrial remnants with natural beauty. A historic smokestack, once part of a glass factory, now serves as an observation tower. Three large lakes were created from former gravel quarries, enhancing the landscape. Walking trails connect various park features and extend to other recreational networks. This adaptive reuse project successfully transformed a deteriorating factory site into a recognizable public space. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Viral Putin, Modi and Xi selfie at BRICS summit is AI-generated
item.description: A viral selfie allegedly showing Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping, Narendra Modi and other leaders together at the BRICS summit in New Delhi is AI-generated. A SynthID watermark shows it was created using OpenAI tools, while several leaders pictured, including Brazil’s Lula and Turkey’s Erdogan, did not attend. Another AI selfie features former Iranian president Ebrahim Raisi, who died in 2024. Both images were widely shared online, including by official embassy accounts. Vedika Bahl fact-checks. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: Vedika BAHL

item.description: China también es consciente de los riesgos de que las máquinas tomen el control humano. El ministro de Seguridad del Estado, Chen Yixin, identificó seis grandes peligros: hipotéticos ataques al régimen, difusión de desinformación, ciberataques a infraestructuras sensibles, revelación de datos personales, entre otros. Aunque Beijing y Washington coinciden en los riesgos de la inteligencia artificial, difieren en las soluciones para evitar una posible crisis tecnológica. item.title: In 2018, Massachusetts removed the first of two old dams from former cranberry bogs; by 2020...
item.description: In a groundbreaking ecological revival, old dams on the Coonamessett River in Massachusetts were dismantled, restoring wetlands and providing passage for migratory fish. This project repurposed industrial farmland into a flourishing coastal ecosystem, allowing fish to ascend to upstream spawning spots that had been blocked for years. The restoration involved creating a sinuous stream channel and replacing a narrow culvert, establishing a model for agricultural bog transformations throughout New England.
